Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zaro (development version)

  • New article, “Connecting to stores” (#4): what to give zaro() for HTTPS, public and private S3, S3-compatible endpoints (including CEPH tenant:bucket names), GCS, GDAL /vsi paths and virtual stores’ references, and a table translating Python’s storage_options.

  • Documentation refresh: the README and pkgdown home page show the current package (plan and fetch, virtual and byterefs stores, sharding, groups, lazy arrays, options); zaro_groups() and zaro_read_arrays() are in the reference index, which fixes the pkgdown build (the site had not deployed since they were added); the DESCRIPTION and help pages no longer say local and cloud stores go through Arrow; the virtual stores article covers flatrefs://.

  • flatrefs:// reads a byterefs flat refs store, the Parquet export that raad.virtualize publishes (arrays.json plus one refs_<array>.parquet per array): synthesised Zarr V2 metadata, codec refusal, coordinates and remap targets as for byterefs://. Chunk references are looked up by reading only the row groups whose dim_k statistics can hold the selection, fetched by byte range through the curl pool and decoded by nanoparquet; the latest getOption("zaro.flat_cache_row_groups", 4) are kept. The Bluelink BRAN2023 temp table (324 MB, 37.5M rows, 36 row groups): the footer in one request (1.2 s), a one-day surface plan reads one 9 MB row group (3.0 s), a point series over every day reads the whole table one batch at a time (33 s, peak 556 MB).

  • Internals for that: parquet-ranged.R reads a Parquet footer by a suffix range request and rewrites it (Thrift compact protocol, top level only) to list some row groups, which then read from a sparse local file. Metadata is read with the file’s num_rows set to 0: nanoparquet 0.5.1 allocates in proportion to it (2.7 GB for 37.5M rows, otherwise).

  • S3 and GCS objects are fetched through the curl pool (#23), as HTTPS, when their access is known: anonymous (anonymous = TRUE, a known public bucket, AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST=YES, options(zaro.cloud_anonymous = TRUE)), or S3 signed by curl’s SigV4 with AWS keys from the environment. This covers native chunks of s3:///gs:// stores (Arrow or GDAL /vsis3/ / /vsigs/) and virtual references to s3:// and gs:// URLs. The bucket region is read once from S3’s x-amz-bucket-region header; endpoint_override / AWS_ENDPOINT_URL give path-style URLs. Other credentials still go through Arrow or GDAL one object at a time. A signed 403 is an error, not an absent chunk. AODN sea level coordinates over s3://: 3.65 s to 0.65 s; CMIP6 GFDL zos coordinates over gs://: 8.37 s to 3.27 s; identical values.

  • The strings-v3.zarr test fixture has consistent dimension names.

  • String data types are read, to character (#22): fixed_length_utf32 (numpy U, V2 <U/>U), null_terminated_bytes (numpy S, V2 |S; alias fixed_length_ascii), and variable-length string with the vlen-utf8 codec (V2 |O with the vlen-utf8 filter), including in shards. String coordinates now load at open: EOPF Sentinel-2 L2A conditions/geometry (angle, band, detector) opens, in zaro and in ndr. zaro_array() refuses string arrays (lazy arrays are numeric or logical) and points to zaro_read(). Tested on stores written by zarr-python 3.2.1.

  • arrow moves from Imports to Suggests (#23). Local stores are read with base R (a new LocalStore), and zstd, gzip and bz2 chunks decode with memDecompress() (falling back to arrow if base R can’t). arrow is still used when installed for s3:// and gs:// stores and for the lz4, brotli and snappy codecs; without it, s3:// and gs:// open through GDAL’s /vsis3/ and /vsigs/ (gdalraster). Imports are now curl, jsonlite, methods, nanoparquet, S7 and utils.

  • future is declared in Suggests (used by the parallel tests).

  • Parquet reference manifests (VirtualiZarr shards, kerchunk Parquet) are read with nanoparquet, not arrow: a virtual store such as BRAN2023 now opens and reads without loading arrow (identical values). nanoparquet reads whole files, which suits sharded manifests (only the shards a selection needs are fetched); for large flat tables arrow’s row-group reads may come back as an option (#23). arrow is still imported for S3/GCS and the Arrow codecs.

  • kerchunk Parquet (reference+parquet://): remote files are downloaded with curl first, rows are classified one by one (a byte reference when the row has a url, else inline data), inline binary values are kept as raw, and the table is parsed without a per-row R loop.

  • New zaro_read_arrays(store, paths): several whole arrays in one fetch. All the arrays’ plans go to one zaro_fetch(), so their HTTP chunks share one connection pool and go out concurrently; each result is identical to zaro_read(). Meant for a dataset’s coordinate arrays at open, where the cost is round trips: two EOPF ECMWF coordinates read in 1.0 s (2.0 s one at a time), AODN’s three in 0.40 s (0.57 s). s3:///gs:// chunks are still fetched one at a time through Arrow.

  • zaro_read()’s chunk assembly is factored out (assemble_chunks()), shared with zaro_read_arrays().

  • zaro_dataset() gains group =, to open the arrays of one group of a nested store, e.g. group = "measurements/reflectance/r10m" of an EOPF Sentinel-2 product. Arrays are named within the group; the dataset records each one’s store path in paths, and zaro_array(), zaro_read() (which now takes a dataset too) and zaro_plan() resolve names through it. The group’s attributes are the dataset’s attributes. Works from consolidated metadata (one request) or by listing.

  • New zaro_groups(): every group of a store with the number of arrays directly in it.

  • V2 consolidated metadata (.zmetadata) now includes nested groups, as V3 consolidated metadata already did.

  • Fix store_list() on Arrow (local, S3, GCS) stores with a non-empty prefix: the root and prefix were joined without a /.

  • byterefs stores: chunk keys are looked up placement first, many at a time (byterefs spec “One chunk by global key”, ported from raad.virtualize mr_chunks()): the array’s placements are read once and kept, matched to the keys, and the chunk rows fetched by primary key. Filtering the refs_<array> view computed every row of the array for each key. At 180k chunk rows one key takes about 3 ms instead of 0.2 s, and 2000 keys about 0.2 s. Results equal the view’s for every key of a test store (absent and inline chunks, non-zero src_offset, a remap target, side-by-side tiles). A store without a placements table falls back to the view.

  • byterefs stores: arrays.codec may be a Zarr V3 codec chain (a JSON array, encode order) or the V2 {compressor, filters} form (decision 0007). The chain is checked (known names, array-to-array then one bytes then bytes-to-bytes, bytes endian agreeing with dtype, no sharding_indexed). An array with a codec zaro does not know is refused: a warning at open, an error on read; the store’s other arrays still read.

  • byterefs stores: a row with offset 0 and size NULL is the whole object at path, and is fetched whole; size NULL with any other offset is an error naming the key (decision 0008).

  • byterefs stores: the Zarr metadata is built once, at open, not for every key.

  • Fix decompression truncating chunks that compress better than 20:1 (zstd, gzip, lz4, brotli, snappy, bz2 through Arrow). The output size was guessed as 20 times the input; constant and all-fill chunks, and mostly-land tiles, compress far beyond that. The stream is now read to the end.

  • New filter imagecodecs_delta (alias horizontal_delta): TIFF predictor 2, horizontal differencing along the last axis with wraparound in the sample’s integer type, as in virtualized COG tiles. Integers up to 32 bits; floating-point predictor 3 is refused clearly. Checked identical to GDAL reading GHRSST MUR COGs through a virtual index.

  • A chunk that fails to decode names its key and byte range, and notes that for a virtual store the source file may have changed after the references were made (they are stale).

  • New exploratory example inst/examples/ghrsst-scratch: GHRSST MUR SST through a draft kerchunk index on source.coop (overview levels as arrays, a full-resolution window checked against GDAL reading the COG).

  • pkgdown site at https://hypertidy.github.io/zaro/, with four articles: getting started (AODN sea level), virtual stores (BRAN2023 via VirtualiZarr, byterefs), planning, fetching and sharding (EOPF Sentinel-2 sharded GeoZarr), and zaro as an ndr engine. The articles are knitted locally from vignettes/articles/*.Rmd.orig so the site builds without network access to the data servers.

  • R CMD check runs on GitHub Actions in the hypertidy/gdal-r-ci images (GDAL release and GDAL HEAD), as for ndr.

  • zaro_plan() columns follow the byterefs view: dim_0, …, dim_{n-1}, present, path, offset, size, data, then zaro’s key and transport. They were url, length, inline and a list column index. The plan’s attribute for the array path is now array (was path, which clashed with the column).

  • byterefs stores: with no target, zaro() applies the store’s meta.default_target (byterefs/spec decision 0004); target = "" reads the verbatim sources, and a target with no remap rules warns. Only the identifiers a byterefs/0.1 reader takes are accepted, byterefs/0.1 and (until byterefs/0.2) mdim-refs/0.2 (decision 0003); another byterefs/ version warns and is read as 0.1. New scheme byterefs://, with mdimrefs:// kept as an alias.

  • Sharded arrays with codecs after sharding_indexed (applied to the whole shard object) now read. A trailing crc32c is skipped and the shard is still read by byte ranges; a compressor means whole shards are fetched and decoded at plan time, and their inner chunks become inline plan rows. These codecs were previously dropped, so such stores failed with length errors. transpose before sharding and nested sharding remain unsupported, with clear errors.

  • A V3 data_type given as an object ({"name": ...}) keeps its name, so unsupported types fail with “unsupported dtype” rather than a class validation error.

  • Acceptance: the EOPF Sentinel-2 L2A sharded GeoZarr on s3.explorer.eopf.copernicus.eu (blosc/zstd inner chunks, index at the end with crc32c) reads identically to zarr-python 3.2.1 and GDAL 3.14; the seven readable sharded fixtures in GDAL’s autotest read as GDAL reads them (tests run when ZARO_GDAL_AUTOTEST or ~/gdal/autotest is found).

  • mdimrefs:// accepts stores stamped byterefs/0.1, the identifier raad.virtualize writes since the format was renamed (byterefs/spec decision 0003), as well as the legacy mdim-refs/0.2. Such stores were refused with “not an mdim-refs store”.

  • Read sharded Zarr V3 arrays (sharding_indexed). A shard is planned as one more level of byte references: zaro_plan() reads the index of each shard a selection touches (one small ranged read per shard, fetched together; a suffix range when the index is at the end) and turns every inner chunk into a byte range of its shard object. Empty inner chunks and missing shards read as fill_value. The index’s crc32c is stripped, not verified. Sharded arrays present their inner chunk shape as the array’s chunks, so zaro_read(), zaro_array() and zaro_chunk() work unchanged; print() of the metadata shows the shard shape. Checked against arrays written by zarr-python 3 (zstd and gzip inner codecs, index at end and start, partially written arrays).

  • A crc32c codec on ordinary chunks is stripped (not verified); it was passed through as an unknown codec.

  • Fix V3 chunk keys: the "v2" chunk key encoding (no c prefix, default separator ".") and the "." separator of the default encoding (c.0.1) were written as c/....

  • New zaro_fetch(store, plan) executes a plan: HTTP references go through one curl connection pool (options(zaro.max_con), default 8, per host and in total), byte ranges that touch on the same URL are merged into one request (options(zaro.merge_gap) widens that), and failed or short responses are retried with backoff. zaro_read() and zaro_array() read through plan + fetch, so every altarr batch is one pooled fetch. The BRAN2023 30-point track reads in 0.9 s (4.8 s one connection at a time); a 60-chunk BRAN2023 surface slice is 2 requests.

  • http:// and https:// stores are read with curl (HttpStore), not gdalraster: GDAL-free, metadata cached, chunks fetched through the pool. An HTTP store can’t be listed, so it needs consolidated metadata (or zaro_dataset(arrays = )). HTTP errors other than not-found are errors, not silently absent chunks. Any /vsi... path opens a gdalraster VSIStore, e.g. zaro("/vsicurl/https://...") to keep GDAL’s HTTP handling.

  • New zaro_plan(): the byte references a selection needs, before any read. One row per chunk with url, offset, length and transport (whole object, byte range in a NetCDF/HDF5 file, inline, or absent), and a printed cost summary (requests, bytes, hosts). Native stores plan with no request; virtual stores read only the manifest they need.

  • Every store now answers store_refs(), and the virtual stores (kerchunk, VirtualiZarr, mdim-refs) fetch through it, so native and virtual reads share one path (“everything is a refs table”).

  • Kerchunk inline chunks prefixed base64: are decoded; references with only a URL read the whole object.

  • byte_range_read() reads local files with base R (no GDAL), and its s3:///gs:// branches return raw vectors (they returned Arrow Buffers).

  • Fix decoding of int64, uint64, uint32 and float16 arrays, which had never been read correctly: the 8- or 4-byte integers were reinterpreted as floating point (e.g. CMIP6 time, stored as int64 hours, read as values like 3.5e-321) and float16 failed. 64-bit integers and uint32 now read as exact doubles (up to 2^53), float16 is decoded from its bit fields, in either byte order.

  • verbose defaults to getOption("zaro.verbose", TRUE) in every function, so options(zaro.verbose = FALSE) silences zaro everywhere; an explicit verbose = still wins.

  • Package source, docs and NEWS are ASCII only.

  • R CMD check is clean: curl, methods and utils are declared in Imports (curl will be the batched fetcher), .github and other dev files are build-ignored, and the track-extract demo moved from inst/demo (a directory R reserves) to inst/examples.

  • Fix remote kerchunk JSON never reading through gdalraster: the VSI file was opened without its path, so the read always failed over to url().

  • parse_zarray() passed an undefined data_type when coercing the fill value; it now passes the parsed dtype.

  • New zaro_dataset(): every array at the root of a store, with dimension names and sizes in R order and the root attributes, read from consolidated metadata in one request (or by listing and probing the store). No data is read. This is the hand-off to ndr’s open_dataset(engine = "zaro").

  • zaro_array() gains cf = TRUE: fill and missing values read as NA, then scale_factor/add_offset are applied per chunk. It also accepts a zaro_dataset in place of a store.

  • Fix consolidated metadata losing numeric precision. Entries were re-serialized with jsonlite’s default of 4 significant digits, so e.g. BRAN2023’s scale_factor of 0.007782219909131527 became 0.0078 and unpacked values were off by up to 0.53 degC. Numbers now round-trip exactly (V2 .zmetadata, V3 consolidated zarr.json, mdim-refs).

  • Fix print methods not being used outside the package: the S7 methods are now registered in .onLoad(), and a stray namespace copy of print no longer captures the S3 registration. Printing an array of a variable-length type (string) no longer errors.

  • New mdimrefs:// source: zaro() reads an mdim-refs SQLite byte-reference table directly, serving Zarr V2 keys from its arrays table and refs_<array> views (target selects a path remap).

  • Fix zaro_read() returning a list-array when fill_value is null. A null fill value (common for coordinate arrays) is now coerced to NA, so reads return a plain numeric array. This also covers the case where a V2 consolidated-metadata round-trip degrades null to an empty object {}, and the V3 path, which previously did not coerce fill_value at all.

  • Add chunk facilities zaro_chunk(), zaro_chunks(), zaro_chunk_apply(), zaro_chunk_info().

  • Fix problem with Arrow decompression (logic was incorrect and hidden in a try/catch).

  • Checks now in place for source strings.

  • Optional validation by reading metadata on connect with zaro() (off by default).

  • Use parallel read with mirai settings for zaro_read.

  • Add helpers for common cases.

  • Improved print for meta group.

  • Fixed egregious error on how to use VSIFile hidden within tryCatch().

  • Add C style orientation (still upside down for ximage).

zaro 0.0.1

Initial version.

Core architecture

  • Arrow-backed Zarr reader for R. Implements the Zarr specification directly using Arrow C++ for filesystem access, compression codecs, and byte buffers. No dependency on zarr-python or any Zarr-specific C/Rust library.

  • S7 class ZaroMeta for parsed array and group metadata, with a uniform representation across Zarr V2 and V3.

  • Store abstraction layer with ArrowStore (local, S3, GCS via Arrow FileSystem), VSIStore (HTTP and fallback S3 via gdalraster), ReferenceStore (Kerchunk JSON references), and VirtualiZarrStore (Parquet manifest reference stores). Designed for future backends (Icechunk) without changing the read pipeline.

  • Codec pipeline normalised across V2 and V3. V2’s single compressor plus filters list is mapped to V3-style codec chains so the decode path is uniform.

Zarr V2 support

  • Parse .zarray, .zgroup, and .zattrs metadata.

  • Consolidated metadata via .zmetadata - a single HTTP request retrieves metadata for all arrays in a V2 store.

  • Numpy dtype string parsing (<f4, >i2, |u1, etc.) with endianness detection.

  • _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS convention for dimension names (xarray compatibility).

  • dimension_separator handling (dot-separated and slash-separated chunk keys).

  • fill_value coercion from JSON strings ("NaN", "Infinity") to R numeric values.

  • sanitize_json() handles Python-flavoured JSON with bare NaN, Infinity, and -Infinity values that are invalid in strict JSON.

Zarr V3 support

  • Parse zarr.json metadata including codecs, dimension names, fill values, and chunk grid configuration.

  • Consolidated V3 metadata (single zarr.json with embedded node metadata).

VirtualiZarr Parquet reference stores

  • New VirtualiZarrStore backend for directory-layout Parquet reference stores as produced by VirtualiZarr. These provide Zarr-style access to existing archival files (NetCDF, HDF5, GRIB) without reformatting.

  • Metadata layer (.zmetadata) fetched via curl - GDAL-free.

  • Chunk manifests (refs.N.parq shards) loaded via arrow::read_parquet() with lazy per-variable loading and environment-based caching.

  • C-order linearization maps chunk grid indices to manifest row positions for stores without explicit chunk key columns.

  • Inline data support via the raw column in manifests (used by coordinate variables whose data is stored directly in the Parquet rather than as byte-range references).

  • Byte-range reads into source files via byte_range_read() supporting Arrow S3/GCS, gdalraster VSI, and curl for HTTP - the full chain is GDAL-free when using curl.

  • URI scheme: virtualizarr://https://example.com/dataset.parq or virtualizarr:///local/path/dataset.parq.

  • Tested against BRAN2023 ocean temperature (5479 time steps, 51 depth levels, 1500x3600 spatial grid, 104 manifest shards, NCI THREDDS byte-range serving).

Cloud access

  • S3 stores via Arrow S3FileSystem with automatic fallback to gdalraster /vsis3/ on 301 region redirects.

  • Anonymous access propagation (anonymous = TRUE maps to AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST for both Arrow and GDAL backends).

  • GCS stores via Arrow GcsFileSystem.

  • HTTP/HTTPS stores via gdalraster /vsicurl/.

Reading

  • Hyperslab reads with start/count indexing (0-based, following Zarr convention).

  • Chunk coverage computation and assembly across chunk boundaries.

  • Blosc (lz4, zstd, zlib, snappy), gzip, and zstd decompression via Arrow codecs.

  • Safety coercion of output array type when fill value would otherwise produce a character array.

Diagnostics

  • Verbose messaging throughout ([zaro] ...), on by default for discoverability. Silence with verbose = FALSE or suppressMessages().

  • Reports store backend, metadata format detected, dtype/shape/chunks/codecs, dimension names, chunk counts during reads.

Tested against

  • AODN cloud-optimised Zarr stores (S3, ap-southeast-2, Zarr V2, blosc/lz4 compression, consolidated .zmetadata).

  • BRAN2023 ocean temperature via VirtualiZarr Parquet references (NCI THREDDS byte-range reads, shuffle+zlib compression, int16 with scale/offset packing).
